industry_prior_art.implication: Do not claim the accessory bundle itself is novel.

candidate_families.name: Conventional reference station

configuration.prep_insert: none or standard loose board as appropriate

questions: What are the task-complete water and hot-water energy baselines?
How much splash reaches predefined clean surfaces?
What are loaded capacity, item-specific dry time and cleaning effort?
candidate_families.exit_gate: Reference performance is repeatable within declared measurement and operator uncertainty.
failure_modes: reference fixture is not representative of the declared use case
meter uncertainty is larger than the candidate/reference effect
task load or procedure drifts across baseline repetitions

candidate_families.name: Retrofit drain-back bridge

configuration.interface: removable rim/edge support selected for one measured reference sink
configuration.drying: vertical-item rack plus removable drip rail that returns water to basin
configuration.repair: replaceable supports, feet, joints and drip rail

questions: Can the rack increase usable loaded capacity without blocking sink tasks?
Can drips return to the basin without splashing or wetting clean items?
Can it be removed quickly for cleaning and stored when not in use?
candidate_families.exit_gate: Loaded stability, drainage, cleaning access and post-cycle geometry meet predeclared limits.

candidate_families.name: Integrated ledge and task-insert station

configuration.basin: one measured single-bowl fixture with cleanable accessory rails

questions: Do inserts reduce transfer distance and free counter area for the declared kitchen layout?
Can inserts be disassembled and cleaned without hidden residue traps?
Does the geometry improve completed-task water, splash and ergonomics versus references?
candidate_families.exit_gate: No cleaning, stability or accessibility hard-gate failure; improvement claims require paired comparisons.

candidate_families.name: Adjustable splash-geometry test rig

configuration.basin: same-size geometry variants or adjustable test basin
configuration.faucet: same faucet or matched measured output across geometry variants
configuration.drying: held constant or excluded during sink-only trials

questions: Which geometry/flow combinations reduce deposition at predefined clean zones?
Does deposition move to the rear wall, faucet, drying rack or another sensitive surface?
Can the geometry still drain and clean easily?
candidate_families.exit_gate: Paired matched-flow trials show reproducible deposition map with no unmeasured relocation.

candidate_families.name: Manual, low-infrastructure station

configuration.power: not required for ordinary use or passive drying
configuration.water_supply: tested across declared variable/low pressure; no claim of operation without a potable supply
configuration.drying: removable passive rack with gravity return
configuration.service: common replaceable seals, aerator, hose and rack wear parts

questions: Does the station remain usable when pressure varies within the declared design range?
Can the user identify and isolate common service faults?
Do common repairs preserve flow, leak-tightness and drainage?
candidate_families.exit_gate: Declared minimum-use envelope and safe service method are documented and validated.

candidate_families.name: Optional low-power drying assist

configuration.prerequisite: Only test after passive rack baseline is repeatable
configuration.air_path: must not draw untreated drain air across clean items
configuration.electrical: requires product-appropriate wet-zone ingress and electrical safety review

questions: Is the reduction in time to the same dryness endpoint worth measured electricity, noise and complexity?
Does the airflow increase tracer deposition or rewetting?
Can the assist module be removed and cleaned?
candidate_families.exit_gate: Passes safety review and demonstrates a preregistered net benefit without unreported trade-offs.

candidate_families.name: Measured-volume batch-wash workflow

configuration.wash_mode: removable, cleanable wash tub or basin plug with visible fill reference; no powered system required
configuration.rinse_mode: separate controlled final-rinse stage with potable water
configuration.intended_initial_track: household use; commercial food-service use requires a separate compliance determination

questions: Does a matched batch-wash workflow use less total water than continuous-flow washing at the same cleaning endpoint?
Does visible, repeatable fill volume reduce user-to-user variability?
What are the ergonomic and spill costs of filling, lifting, draining and cleaning the tub?
failure_modes: reuse dirty wash water for final rinse
soil transfer increases between items as wash water becomes loaded
batch volume not measured and candidates start with unequal water
unsafe lifting or tipping of a heavy filled tub
insert traps soil, leaks, or blocks primary drain
household workflow is assumed compliant for regulated food-service warewashing
candidate_families.exit_gate: Matched physical trials show lower task water without cleaning/rewash regression; handling, drain, cleanability and use-case compliance gates pass.

candidate_families.name: Force-qualified commercial pre-rinse sprayer

configuration.nozzle: replaceable, mechanically controlled nozzle and trigger
configuration.validation_scope: separate commercial pre-rinse fixture; do not pool household sink/rack data
configuration.control: manual, no network or powered function required for ordinary operation
configuration.service: replaceable nozzle/seals/trigger with post-service flow/force/coverage check

questions: What water and trigger time achieve a matched soil-removal endpoint?
Can adequate force and coverage be maintained across the declared flowing-pressure envelope?
Does an efficiency improvement persist under realistic trigger patterns and nozzle wear?
failure_modes: lower flow causes longer trigger-on time and more total water
force passes at one pressure but fails elsewhere in the declared envelope
central force looks adequate while edge coverage misses soil
soil-removal average conceals a difficult-soil failure
spray relocates tracer deposition onto clean food-contact surfaces
nozzle wear or clogging degrades results after initial trial
household sink results are incorrectly pooled with commercial pre-rinse trials
candidate_families.exit_gate: Matched commercial task trials meet the preregistered soil-removal endpoint across the required pressure envelope; water, splash, effort, service and applicable product-compliance gates are not regressed.

staged_experiment: Stage 0: select a common purchasable baseline and document all relevant geometry and ratings.
Stage 1: establish baseline repeatability for task litres, temperature/energy, cleaning endpoint, splash and drying.
Stage 2: screen P1 retrofit and P3 splash geometry independently before custom basin tooling.
Stage 3: combine only improvements that survived their independent hard gates into P2 integrated station.
Stage 4: evaluate P4 in a separately declared variable-pressure and accessibility profile.
Stage 5: test P5 only if passive drying leaves a clear, measured gap worth addressing.
Stage 6: compare candidates on a Pareto frontier; publish failed profiles, uncertainty and test deviations.
